open_material_decisions: What exact farewell line should be added, and should it always appear as a new line after the greeting when enabled?

question.prompt: This changes the exact observable output and acceptance tests. Choose the farewell line behavior when the optional farewell is enabled.

options.label: New line: Goodbye!
options.description: Append a second line exactly `Goodbye!` after the greeting; simplest and most judgeable.

options.label: Same line: Goodbye!
options.description: Append ` Goodbye!` on the same line as the greeting; shorter output but different formatting contract.

options.label: Custom text/placement
options.description: Provide your own exact farewell text and whether it appears on a new line or the same line.

answer:
When enabled, append a second line immediately after the greeting line. The farewell line is exactly `Goodbye.`. The greeting remains the first line.

Activation: controlled only by `includeFarewell`; default `false` when omitted.

Examples:
- `name=Sam, includeFarewell=true` -> `Hello, Sam!\nGoodbye.`
- `name=Sam, includeFarewell=false` -> `Hello, Sam!`

interviewer.reason: The only material ambiguity was the exact farewell output shape and activation rule. The transcript confirms the farewell text, placement, and control flag, and no further material decision is required to make the requirement judgeable and implementation-ready.

contract.summary: Add an optional farewell line to the text-only greeter. The greeting must remain the first line. When `includeFarewell` is `true`, append a second line immediately after the greeting line containing exactly `Goodbye.`. When `includeFarewell` is `false` or omitted, do not append any farewell line.
confirmed_decisions: Output order: the greeting is always the first line.
Farewell placement: when enabled, the farewell appears on a second line immediately after the greeting.
Farewell text: the farewell line is exactly `Goodbye.`
Activation rule: the farewell is controlled only by `includeFarewell`.
Default behavior: if `includeFarewell` is omitted, treat it as `false`.
Example with farewell present: `name=Sam, includeFarewell=true` produces `Hello, Sam!\nGoodbye.`
Otherwise similar example with farewell absent: `name=Sam, includeFarewell=false` produces `Hello, Sam!`
acceptance_checks: Given `name=Sam` and `includeFarewell=true`, output is exactly `Hello, Sam!\nGoodbye.`
Given `name=Sam` and `includeFarewell=false`, output is exactly `Hello, Sam!`
Given `name=Sam` and omitted `includeFarewell`, output is exactly `Hello, Sam!`
When farewell is enabled, no extra blank line appears between greeting and farewell.
When farewell is disabled or omitted, no farewell text appears anywhere in the output.
